High Cost Oral Atypical Antipsychotics (Bysanti, Caplyta, Cobenfy, Fanapt, Lybalvi, Rexulti, 
Vraylar) 
 
  
  
Prior Authorization Guideline 
 
  
Guideline ID 
GL-722200  
Guideline Name 
High Cost Oral Atypical Antipsychotics (Bysanti, Caplyta, Cobenfy, 
Fanapt, Lybalvi, Rexulti, Vraylar)  
Formulary 
• 
Medicaid - Community & State Arizona  
 
 
Guideline Note: 
Effective Date: 
10/18/2026  
 
 
 
 
1 .  Criteria 
 
Product Name:Vraylar  
Diagnosis 
Schizophrenia  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Diagnosis of schizophrenia  


--- PDF page 814 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 814 
 
AND 
 
2 - Patient is 13 years of age or older  
 
AND 
 
3 - ONE of the following:  
 
 3.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to ONE of the following:  
• 
Aripiprazole  
• 
Clozapine  
• 
Olanzapine  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Risperidone  
• 
Ziprasidone  
 
OR 
 
 3.2 Contraindication to ALL of the following:  
• 
Aripiprazole  
• 
Clozapine  
• 
Olanzapine  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Risperidone  
• 
Ziprasidone  
 
OR 
 
 3.3 The patient has been receiving treatment with the requested medication and is new to the 
plan (enrollment effective date within the past 90 days)  
 
OR 
 
 3.4 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge  
 


--- PDF page 815 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 815 
Product Name:Bysanti, Caplyta, Fanapt, Lybalvi, Rexulti  
Diagnosis 
Schizophrenia  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Diagnosis of schizophrenia  
 
AND 
 
2 - ONE of the following:  
 
 2.1 If the request is for Rexulti, patient is 13 years of age or older  
 
OR 
 
 2.2 If the request is for Bysanti, Caplyta, Fanapt, or Lybalvi, patient is 18 years of age or 
older  
 
AND 
 
3 - ONE of the following:  
 
 3.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to TWO of the following:  
• 
Aripiprazole  
• 
Clozapine  
• 
Olanzapine  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Risperidone  
• 
Ziprasidone  
 
OR 
 
 3.2 Contraindication to ALL of the following:  


--- PDF page 816 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 816 
• 
Aripiprazole  
• 
Clozapine  
• 
Olanzapine  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Risperidone  
• 
Ziprasidone  
 
OR 
 
 3.3 The patient has been receiving treatment with the requested medication and is new to the 
plan (enrollment effective date within the past 90 days)  
 
OR 
 
 3.4 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge  
 
AND 
 
4 - If the request is for Lybalvi, ONE of the following:  
 
 4.1 Patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2 or greater  
 
OR 
 
 4.2 Patient has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater with a weight-related comorbidity (e.g., 
dyslipidemia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea)  
 
OR 
 
 4.3 Patient has a documented history of weight gain of greater than or equal to 10% of their 
baseline weight after initiating antipsychotic medication  
 
OR 


--- PDF page 817 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 817 
 
 4.4 Physician has provided clinical rationale for requiring samidorphan in addition to 
olanzapine therapy  
 
AND 
 
5 - If the request is for Bysanti, history of failure to Fanapt  
 
Product Name:Cobenfy  
Diagnosis 
Schizophrenia  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Diagnosis of schizophrenia  
 
AND 
 
2 - ONE of the following:  
 
 2.1 BOTH of the following:  
 
  2.1.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial), adverse reaction, or contraindication to 
aripiprazole  
 
AND 
 
  2.1.2 ONE of the following:  
 
   2.1.2.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to ONE of the 
following: 
• 
Clozapine  
• 
Olanzapine  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Risperidone  


--- PDF page 818 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 818 
• 
Ziprasidone  
 
OR 
 
   2.1.2.2 Contraindication to ALL of the following: 
• 
Clozapine  
• 
Olanzapine  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Risperidone  
• 
Ziprasidone  
 
OR 
 
 2.2 The patient has been receiving treatment with the requested medication and is new to the 
plan (enrollment effective date within the past 90 days)  
 
OR 
 
 2.3 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge

AND 
 
2 - Patient is 10 years of age or older

AND

AND 
 
3 - ONE of the following:  
 
 3.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to THREE of the 
following:  
• 
Aripiprazole  
• 
Lamotrigine  
• 
Lithium  
•

OR 
 
 3.4 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge  
 
AND 
 
4 - If the request is for Lybalvi, ONE of the following:  
 
 4.1 Patient has a body mass index (BMI) of 30 kg/m2 or greater  
 
OR 
 
 4.2 Patient has a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater with a weight-related comorbidity (e.g., 
dyslipidemia, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, sleep apnea)  
 
OR 
 
 4.3 Patient has a documented history of weight gain of greater than or equal to 10% of their

OR

olanzapine therapy  
 
AND

UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 822 
Product Name:Vraylar  
Diagnosis 
Bipolar Depression  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Diagnosis of bipolar depression  
 
AND 
 
2 - ONE of the following:  
 
 2.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to ONE of the following:  
• 
Lurasidone  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Olanzapine plus fluoxetine  
• 
Valproate monotherapy  
• 
Combination Therapy (i.e., lithium plus lamotrigine/valproate, lurasidone plus 
lithium/valproate, quetiapine plus lithium/valproate)  
 
OR 
 
 2.2 Contraindication to ALL of the following:  
• 
Lurasidone  
• 
Quetiapine  
• 
Olanzapine plus fluoxetine  
• 
Valproate monotherapy  
• 
Combination Therapy (i.e., lithium plus lamotrigine/valproate, lurasidone plus 
lithium/valproate, quetiapine plus lithium/valproate)  
 
OR 
 
 2.3 The patient has been receiving treatment with the requested medication and is new to the 
plan (enrollment effective date within the past 90 days)  


--- PDF page 823 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 823 
 
OR 
 
 2.4 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge

•

• 
Lurasidone  
•

•

Combination Therapy (i.e., lithium plus lamotrigine/valproate, lurasidone plus

 2.4 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital

Product Name:Vraylar  
Diagnosis 
Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Diagnosis of ONE of the following:  
• 
Major depressive disorder (MDD)  
• 
Treatment resistant depression  
 
AND 
 
2 - ONE of the following:  
 
 2.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to TWO different 
antidepressants from the following classes (antidepressants MUST be from TWO different 
classes):  
• 
Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)  
• 
Serotonin Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (SNRIs)  
• 
New Generation Antidepressants (e.g., bupropion, mirtazapine, etc)  


--- PDF page 825 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 825 
• 
Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs)  
 
OR 
 
 2.2 The patient has been receiving treatment with the requested medication and is new to the 
plan (enrollment effective date within the past 90 days)  
 
OR 
 
 2.3 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge  
 
Product Name:Caplyta, Rexulti  
Diagnosis 
Major Depressive Disorder (MDD)  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - Diagnosis of major depressive disorder (MDD)  
 
AND 
 
2 - ONE of the following:  
 
 2.1 BOTH of the following:  
 
  2.1.1 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to TWO different 
antidepressants from the following classes (antidepressants MUST be from TWO different 
classes):  
• 
Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)  
• 
Serotonin Norepinephrine Reuptake Inhibitors (SNRIs)  
• 
New Generation Antidepressants (e.g., bupropion, mirtazapine, etc)  
• 
Tricyclic Antidepressants (TCAs)  


--- PDF page 826 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 826 
 
AND 
 
  2.1.2 Inadequate response (minimum 30 day trial) or adverse reaction to TWO of the 
following:  
• 
Aripiprazole  
• 
Quetiapine ER  
• 
Risperidone  
• 
Augmented Therapy (e.g., addition of lithium, another antidepressant from a different 
class, thyroid hormone to current antidepressant regimen)  
 
OR 
 
 2.2 The patient has been receiving treatment with the requested medication and is new to the 
plan (enrollment effective date within the past 90 days)  
 
OR 
 
 2.3 The patient is currently receiving treatment with the requested medication in the hospital 
and must continue upon discharge  
 
Product Name:Rexulti  
Diagnosis 
Agitation Associated with Dementia Due to Alzheimer's Disease  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Prior Authorization  
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - The requested medication is being used for treatment of agitation associated with 
dementia due to Alzheimer's disease  
 
Product Name:Bysanti, Caplyta, Cobenfy, Fanapt, Lybalvi, Rexulti, Vraylar  
Approval Length 
12 month(s)  
Guideline Type 
Quantity Limit  


--- PDF page 827 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 827 
 
 
Approval Criteria    
 
1 - ONE of the following:  
 
 1.1 The requested drug must be used for a Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved 
indication  
 
OR 
 
 1.2 The use of this drug is supported by information from ONE of the following appropriate 
compendia of current literature:  
• 
Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved indications and limits  
• 
Published practice guidelines and treatment protocols  
• 
Comparative data evaluating the efficacy, type and frequency of side effects and 
potential drug interactions among alternative products as well as the risks, benefits, 
and potential patient outcomes  
• 
Drug Facts and Comparisons  
• 
American Hospital Formulary Service Drug Information  
• 
United States Pharmacopeia - Drug Information  
• 
DRUGDEX Information System  
• 
UpToDate  
• 
MicroMedex  
• 
Peer-reviewed medical literature, including randomized clinical trials, outcomes, 
research data, and pharmacoeconomic studies  
• 
Other drug reference resources  
 
AND 
 
2 - ONE of the following:  
 
 2.1 The drug is being prescribed within the manufacturer’s published dosing guidelines  
 
OR 
 
 2.2 The requested dose falls within dosing guidelines found in ONE of the following 
compendia of current literature:  
• 
Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved indications and limits  
• 
Published practice guidelines and treatment protocols  


--- PDF page 828 ---
UnitedHealthcare Community Plan of Arizona – Clinical Pharmacy Guidelines 
Page 828 
• 
Comparative data evaluating the efficacy, type and frequency of side effects and 
potential drug interactions among alternative products as well as the risks, benefits, 
and potential patient outcomes  
• 
Drug Facts and Comparisons  
• 
American Hospital Formulary Service Drug Information  
• 
United States Pharmacopeia - Drug Information  
• 
DRUGDEX Information System  
• 
UpToDate  
• 
MicroMedex  
• 
Peer-reviewed medical literature, including randomized clinical trials, outcomes, 
research data, and pharmacoeconomic studies  
• 
Other drug reference resources  
 
AND 
 
3 - The requested dosage cannot be achieved using the plan accepted quantity limit of a 
different dose or formulation  
 
AND 
 
4 - The drug is being prescribed for a medically accepted indication that is recognized as a 
covered benefit by the applicable health plans’ program  
 
AND 
 
5 - Physician has provided rationale for needing to exceed the quantity limit (QL) of ONE of 
the following:  
• 
For Caplyta requests, QL of 1 capsule/day  
• 
For Cobenfy capsule requests, QL of 2 capsules/day  
• 
For Cobenfy starter pack requests, QL of 2 packs/365 days  
• 
For Bysanti and Fanapt tablet requests, QL of 2 tablets/day  
• 
For Bysanti and Fanapt titration pack requests, QL of 1 pack/180 days  
• 
For Lybalvi requests, QL of 1 tablet/day  
• 
For Rexulti requests, QL of 1 tablet/day  
• 
For Vraylar 0.5 mg, 0.75 mg, 4.5 mg and 6 mg requests, QL of 1 capsule/day  
• 
For Vraylar 1.5 mg and 3 mg requests, QL of 2 capsules/day  
• 
For Vraylar therapy pack requests, 2 packs/365 days
